title: Inside the VM: one tree, two disks, the notes on the data disk
subtitle: Linux has no C: or D:. The data disk is hung on the folder /mnt/data, Docker is told to live there, and a throwaway container packs the volume for the backup.

notes.text:
Mounting = hanging a disk on a folder of the one tree. After step 1, anything written under /mnt/data lands on the 32 GB data disk; everything else stays on the OS disk.

Restore is the same road backwards: download the .tar.gz, let Compose make an empty notes_data, unpack it with tar xzf, start postgres. You get back what was there when the backup was made.

# 1. /etc/fstab
UUID=3f6c2b1e-...  /mnt/data  ext4  defaults,nofail  0  2

# 2. /etc/docker/daemon.json
{ "data-root": "/mnt/data/docker" }
# /etc/containerd/config.toml, first line
root = "/mnt/data/containerd"

# 4. pack the volume (db stopped)
docker run --rm -v notes_data:/data:ro \
  -v /mnt/data/backups:/backup alpine \
  tar czf /backup/notes-data.tar.gz -C /data .
# 5. send it out
az storage blob upload --auth-mode login ...
